title: Big downgrade since version 3
body: I used to really love this app. It was the best way to organize recipes and shopping lists. Ever since the 3.0 update, it’s gotten much worse. I will give one example to illustrate, but please understand that it represents more issues. In the shopping list page I want to rename my list. There are two icons that have three dots in them. Bot of them bring up the same menu of options (which has its own issues) but the menu doesn’t contain an option to rename the shopping list. (Why are there two buttons for the same menu to begin with?) There is another button of three lines in the upper left, so I’ll try that. That brings up the master menu for the app, which is already somewhat duplicated in the bottom bar, and it doesn’t have the option to rename the menu. There is a pencil icon too - maybe that’s what I’m looking for? No that’s for selecting items in the list. Finally there is an icon in the upper right that has three lines. That one brings up the list of all my shopping lists. Each of which has another menu icon next to it. That’s the one I have to tap on to rename the menu. But Please note!! I don’t mean to say that you should fix this one thing and the app will be fine, what I mean to illustrate is a pervasive sense of lack of user experience. I’m very disappointed because I expected to use this app for a long time, and it was relatively expensive for the lifetime membership. Honestly if I could revert to version 2.2.295 I would.

title: Absolute trash!

title: The new update is awful
body: September 2025 update: so I’m back, and have lowered my review from 2 stars down to 1 star. I can only imagine they had to appease investors or something, for the way they’ve absolutely wrecked their app. Adding a text recipe is very clunky, when it should be arguably the easiest thing to do: The very first thing that comes up is an ingredients window. Uh ok. So you type out the ingredients and then click a green check with the word “Confirm.” A green check mark with the word “confirm” implies completion. It tells the user “click here when you’re done,” however, on Cookbook, it means “proceed to the next section.” That’s confusing. So now onto the next section …which is a disorganized, visually noisy page, where you can finally add a recipe title, add tags, a has a big annoying purple button to add an AI IMAGE (what???) Now where do I add the instructions? Oh. There it is. A very small, out of the way section toward the bottom. Onto notes: on recipes, you can put little notes for yourself, that will appear on the main page of the recipe when you open it. Did you know you had to press and drag, and that there is an invisible bar on the side? Neither did it. They have compressed the notes section so only a very small section of your notes will show, and start to gray out/disappear toward the bottom. You’ll instinctively try to tap on it, thinking it will expand the text. Nothing. You will have to tap press hold and drag and a little side scroll will magically appear to let you scroll through your notes. Again, not intuitive. You guys I’m sorry and I know you’re going to double down on this but… this update is not meant for those of us who were there from the beginning. Those of us who paid for the app, and dedicated hours, who used this in our professional kitchens and offices with staff. This app was made to impress someone (who? Teens on TikTok?) with jazzy AI features and a completely disorganized and not UI friendly structure.

title: Investigation of a Viable App for Capturing Recipes From Numerous Sources
body: As the title suggests, I sought a reliable application capable of capturing recipes from diverse sources. Initially, I was enthusiastic about this app upon discovering it. However, after reading reviews from satisfied lifetime subscribers, my excitement transformed into dismay. As an experienced software quality professional, I must express my profound disappointment with your response regarding lifetime subscribers’ need to contact you for subscription reactivation. A software update should have automatically restored all lifetime subscribers to active status without additional contact with your administrative staff. The fact that this did not occur indicates significant flaws in your software upgrade management process, particularly in the areas of requirement definition, user profile status, integration, and testing. Alternatively, it is possible that the company intentionally proceeded with this strategy to manipulate lifetime subscribers into purchasing memberships again through individuals who were unaware of the issue or simply apathetic and unwilling to navigate the administrative process you described in your responses to their complaints. Initially, I had no intention on addressing this issue by the overwhelming number of complaints received prompted me to address this matter as a senior member of the community. I understand that many seniors may not possess the necessary knowledge to question the update, prefer not to engage in the hassle, or simply choose to disregard the issue altogether.

title: Theft!
body: I paid to own this app outright precisely to avoid getting sucked into a money pit: years of investments in a niche personal tool that does one little thing. Now I’m being told that I will be unable to continue using the app going forward, except in read-only mode after one year of “free” subscription. The problem is twofold: (1) I relied on the nature of an outright purchase and have not been in a hurry to digitize recipes, so I have very little content to date. So I will basically have gifted the developers my money for a loan rather than a purchase. SaaS is a loan. No thank you. (2) The app, if I do rush to fill it with content now, will be useless for the very reason I bought it in the first place: data consolidation. The last thing I want is recipes spread across different apps. Should I never add another app to my personal catalog again? Or should I waste my time and homescreen space switching between catalogs? Both are terrible options. This is, frankly, fraud and theft. I paid for X and you are taking it away and replacing it with Y. I do not consent. Why not just grandfather legacy users into lifetime plans?

title: Absolutely horrendous OCR. I feel scammed.
body: I don’t understand how in 2020 this app can even advertise that it has OCR when it’s as bad as it is. 1) you CANNOT take a picture from the app. Sure, they say you can, but they don’t use any image stabilization like your camera does. So it’ll be blurry EVERY time and make the already garbage OCR even more garbage. If you have a tripod and remote (so you can stand on the other side of the room and not breathe nearby) you may be able to get a clear picture with their camera function. Otherwise, forget about it. 2) you have to go select the sections and tell the app where everything goes. Okay, not a huge deal - in fact I prefer when apps rely more on the user when they definitely are bad at particular functions. Problem is - CookBook App wants to make the selection process as miserable as possible. You can only resize using ONE of the four corners of the selection box. So you’re constantly resizing, then moving, then resizing again, moving again, until you get it to the right size and shape using your ONE corner. 3) once you’ve resized your box to the perfect size using your ONE corner, understand that you cannot have a single extra letter in the box. Because if you do, it’s going into the recipe. Oh - and remember - since you only have one point to resize from, your selection box has to be a perfect rectangle. Which means your photo has to be of a perfectly flat page. Which means you’re either printing your recipe (in which case, download direct from browser and forget OCR) or you’re ripping out pages from your cookbook (definitely bad idea). The entire point of OCR is to import recipes from COOKBOOKS and pages of books don’t lie perfectly flat. So you’re screwed. 4) let’s say you’re fine with all that and you go for it anyway. Well, guess what, this app’s OCR can’t detect COLUMNS. Have you ever seen a recipe that doesn’t use multiple columns? I haven’t. So every single line it goes alllllll the way across from column 1 to column 2 to column 3 and so on until it reaches the end of your carefully crafted selection box and then it skips all the way back to column 1. I guess you could add additional selection boxes to try and mitigate this, but honestly at that point I was done with it. 5) oh - I almost forgot - it can’t detect fractions. AT ALL. So 1 1/2 becomes 14. Why the hell it becomes 14 and not 112 or something dumb like that I have no idea. So you also can plan to go manually update every single fraction in the recipe. No big deal - it’s not like many recipes use fractions, right? You’re way better off just going to an app that actually uses decent OCR technology like Google any paying up. OR go to an app optimized for manual recipe input and just do it that way. I bought this app specifically because it advertised OCR and it is so incredibly bad that I feel like I was completely scammed and that it’s not even fair to claim they have OCR when it is so impractical and essentially non-functional. Oh well... at least it only cost me $4.99 to realize this isn’t better than the recipe manager app I already had.

title: Recent convert from Pepperplate
body: Several years ago I became a big fan of online/digital recipe managers and weekly meal planners. For many years, I used Pepperplate, which was free, and I enjoyed it greatly. However, no updates were being performed and performance was dwindling and then they instituted a $3 monthly fee, so it was time to make the switch. I spent several days researching before deciding that CookBook had most of the features I wanted. I have been using this app for nearly 3 months now, slowly importing my 200+ recipe database I had created in Pepperplate. I really like the ease of importing recipes from the web. It imports photos, which Pepperplate never did, so that’s great. I also like that the list of ingredients shows on the left while you can scroll through the recipe steps on the right of the screen. Easily adjusting the recipe for the number of servings and between imperial or metric or US conversions is helpful. The app has a nice, clean, aesthetic and fits with my style. It is pleasing to the eye and to my utilitarian nature. Importing from Pepperplate via .txt files works okay, but several fields don’t import so I have chosen to pay for a few months of Pepperplate service just to make sure all my data transfers completely. I do not use the grocery list portion of the app because I have another app I already use for that task and prefer. I am looking forward to when the website is updated to function as well as the tablet and phone apps. I like sitting down at my computer for menu planning. I would also like to see the ability to easily “swap” recipes from one day to another by simply clicking and dragging on the web browser, or within the app, to choose which day and meal to swap a recipe. This was available in Pepperplate. Another helpful feature that I like within Pepperplate that I don’t see in CookBook is the ability to plan a meal that I corporates a few recipes. For example: I make spaghetti and meatballs for dinner one night and I have a recipe for the sauce and one for the meatballs. I would like to create a meal that had both recipes so that then I can simple add that meal to the planner and both recipes automatically appear. This same feature would meet my need for menu items for “leftovers” or “dinner out” rather than creating a blank recipe. These few suggestions are the only ways that I see that CookBook could be improved. These few improvements are the only reason for 4 instead of 5 stars for my review. Also, the customer service seems to be great. I emailed with a question and got a reply within 24 hours. This is of high value to me. Thanks for creating this great app! I look forward to using it for many years to come.

I finally had my first issue this week when I got a new iPad that came with iOS 26 - the app would crash as soon as I tried to open it. I sent a message to the developers who responded promptly (shout out to Sammy!) and were very friendly. Since they store all of my recipes on their end, I was able to safely follow their guidance to remove the app, then reinstall it. The whole process took less than a minute and my recipes loaded in immediately. If you’re thinking about getting this app, go on…do it…pull that trigger - trust me, it’s worth every penny and then some!

title: Pretty easy to import and organize all my recipes

I exported my old cookbook to a pdf and have been importing from that file one by one (no bulk import, a feature I’d REALLY like). Taking photos of some recipes, finding the online origin of others and using a URL, makes for easy going. Aside from a bulk import, the other missing feature is the ability to print out my recipes in a nice format with an index. Overall, a good CookBook app to switch to.

title: Best Cookbook App
body: I have used several apps in the past but found this one and it has been the best. This app makes it so easy to add new recipes with either a photo or importing off of other social media platforms and also just typing in a new recipe. I did the one year subscription and have really enjoyed using it. I will definitely be renewing. I also have had no troubles with it glitching or freezing while using. Highly recommend

title: Best recipe app
body: My review is below BUT I have one suggestion- allow someone’s recipes to be shared with another user. I’ve done all the hard work and would like to pass on to others in my family. I’ve been using this app for about 8-9 years and have seen it continuously improve! I’ve been able to take all my family recipes on 3x5 cards, plus recipes I’ve found & loved online.

title: Best recipe manager I have seen
body: I had a different recipe manager for probably 10 years. I was happy with it as it met the need. Over the years I had accumulated over 500 recipes. A few months ago I decided to pay for the cloud service that allowed me to access recipes on other devices. Imagine my chagrin when the syncing stopped after the last IOS update. When I looked back at the app version info I was stunned to see that the last update was 2 years ago. Now there is no way to contact the developer or customer support as the website won’t come up.” And it’s still available for downloading in the App Store. Stupid me for paying for the cloud service subscription through 2020 (seems like fraud to me) Anyway, found the Cook Book app and I love it. I have transferred all my recipes and love the automatic syncing from my IPad to IPhone. And I love the features. If you’re looking for a great recipe manager, this is the one to get!!

title: Great app for organizing your recipes
body: This app is incredible. The import options are amazing. I have a book with handwritten recipes, some basically scribbles. The OCR algorithm imports the text almost flawlessly. Usually just 1 or 2 minor corrections. The imports from websites are just as amazing. It cuts through all the fluff and finds the ingredients and instructions and “poof”! It’s all there and ready to save. Also their support is first class. I had an issue with the recipe resizing feature when they did their recent upgrade and they had a fix for me the same day. Wow! Totally impressed with this app.

title: WOW! Upgraded version is fantastic!
body: I had been using Cookbook Manager for the last few years. Recently, the icon changed from blue to orange, and I braced myself. I was not a fan at first and then I realized everything that it now does - including uploading recipes directly from TikTok and Facebook. It’s fan-freaking-tastic!! BIG LOVE!! 1000/10

title: Update: Asked and answered! Original:Remove review prompts!
body: Update: Thank you so much for the quick response and resolution of the review prompt rapid fire bug! I love all the new features from the update; they have made an already 5* app even better!! title: Fantastic
body: Thankyou for this amazing helpmate. I am just loving how quick and easy to keep and add recipes and shop. I have tried other apps but this one is the best hands down. Always so helpful and you respond quickly to my questions. What a great app!!!🌴

title: ADHD Friendly
body: I have now been using this app for over 2 years now. I cannot read recipes in any other format, I just can’t focus. All the recipes online flood you with adds and other recipe suggestions causing too much noise. Just import the recipe into the cook book and it turns it into a clean, organized, streamlined format that’s easy to read! And you can cross off the completed tasks! And now with the new update, the ingredients are highlighted in the steps! My brain is so happy! With every update it just keeps getting better!

title: Update makes a big difference
body: I’ve been using this program for over a year and really liked it before, but with the new update, I can take advantage of AI to select the recipe tags and provide a very good photo. The search function remains really good and has been accurate even tho’ I’ve misspelled a few recipe titles. I also commend the program team for being very responsive to questions. title: Simple and easy
body: I have tried a lot of different recipe apps and this is by far the best!! Inserting your own recipe is so simple and everything is laid out exactly how I would want a cookbook to. Also importing from the internet or social media is amazing! I have never had to edit an imported recipe, it gets it perfectly from the source. I definitely recommend this app

title: Best Recipe App Ever
body: I’ve been using this app since January to keep track of all my recipes. The recipe import feature makes life easy. I used to spend forever reading articles, but now I can just paste them into the app and get the same format each time. Five stars before the update, but now that they’ve added the Ai feature it’s even better. Sometimes I want to send a recipe to a friend/family member, so I print off a pdf version straight from the app and send it to them. Super easy. Great Job Cook Book team, keep it up!

title: Loved it until the update
body: I’ve been using CookBook for years and bought the lifetime membership. Has been my consistent go to for downloading and storing recipes. Unfortunately, the most recent update completely overhauled the app and has made downloading recipes incredibly more difficult. We’ll, it’s kinda broke now….:-(

title: Cookbook Keeps Getting Better
body: I discovered Cookbook several years ago and loved its versatility then, but with its recent relaunch it has gotten even better. Now it is easy to download recipes from virtually every social media platform which is huge. They even have figured out how to use AI to search for a recipe from a mere photo. I can’t wait to try it at my favorite restaurant! Keep up the great work Team Cookbook!!!

title: Started out great, the update is even better
body: This app is so well designed, functionally and visually. Easy to use, organize, update, take notes, and track your recipe. I use the import feature ALL the time and was thrilled to see new ways to add recipes in the update. And the update! Loved the old version and wasn’t excited about the update, but guys. They did amazing. More features, but easier to use, with better menus and more interesting, straightforward ways to scroll and search your recipes. Fantastic job to the developer team, this is one of my most used apps. Thank you!!

title: Love this app.
body: I have never been so excited about an app before. All my recipes are in one place 👏. Copying and transferring recipes is a breeze. I copied a recipe from a magazine while waiting at my dentist's office. I will love it even more if it offers something like the featured recipe of the day. It still gets five stars. I have a question: do the lifetime subscription has limited content?

title: Wow! A must have!
body: I have had this app for a long time, so long that I bought a lifetime membership when it was available. I absolutely loved it then, never did I ever think I would love it even more. This new update is AMAZING! And makes getting recipes from TikTok, Facebook and online so much easier now! The ability to get recipes that are accurate from TikTok is top notch!

title: Best $ spent
body: I don’t leave reviews. But this app is so good I wanted to share my experience with it. I’ve been using it for several years, and it just keeps getting better. I tried a bunch of other recipe apps, but they all were missing features, which made them clunky and not enjoyable to use. Cookbook seems like it is designed by people who actually cook in their kitchens. I love using it so much that I immediately import any paper recipes I’m even considering trying. The scanning is so smart it’s a breeze. The app also has the ability to set multiple timers for different steps or different recipes, and any time that shows up in a recipe can be turned into a timer just with a tap. I could go on and on, but you should just try it!

title: New update is terrible
body: I’ve used this app for years. It was always a little quirky but the new update makes it almost unreadable. None of the links I want to paste are working.

title: A must for avid cooks
body: I got this app several years ago and have fallen in love with it. I used to use Pinterest but found that being unable to make notes or save changes I made to recipes wasn’t working for me. This app curates my recipes in a similar way, keeps links to the original recipe, and allows me the freedom to edit recipes according to personal preferences.

title: Everything I wished for
body: I have been using the CookBook app for about 10 years and have loved it from the start. The ability to import recipes from websites, cookbooks, or handwritten notes; the ease of sharing and printing; tagging, scaling, meal planning, viewing recipes in tiles; the portability, offline functionality, smooth navigation, filtering - and so much more. All of this in one app, when many others fell short. Over time, I started missing a nutrition calculator and the ability to import directly from TikTok, Pinterest, or Instagram, but I stayed because of the app’s many strengths and the fact that all my recipes were in it. The latest release now has everything I ever wished for. I am so, so pleased.This is truly the best cooking app out there. Well done!

title: Great recipe app
body: Easy to use, fast importing from recipe sites, lots of helpful features. Very responsive customer service.

title: Obsessed
body: I have had this app since 2019, and I am an avid user. The latest update… all I can say is BRAVO. With the AI and new integration features, it’s even more amazing, accessible, and intelligent. The way the app scans recipes is second to none - I’ve tried others to make sure I’ve got the best one for me, there is no competition. Logical timers in the app tagged with the recipe, ease of switching back and forth between recipes, smart grocery lists, and now the AI overlay… I love this app. Thank you for making my life easier.

title: WOW!!! You all have been BUSY!! This looks A-MAZ-ING!!!

title: Amazing!
body: Absolutely love this app. Now all my recipes can be in one place. I literally recommend this app to everyone now. Hope it never goes away. Best app for storing recipes!!!

title: Loyal user for 6 years
body: My husband and I bought this app several years ago in response to several arguments we would have about the mental load of meal planning. It is now the saving grace for our sanity. No more shuffling through recipe binders, no more scrolling through online recipe blogs, no more scatterbrained grocery lists. body: I hunted for a good recipe app that did what I needed. One app that widened across all my devices, from my iPhone to my Samsung fridge smart display, that didn’t charge me extra between devices. I wanted something that could scan from books but also websites. I wanted something to help me store recipes from my grandparents. THIS IS IT. It’s everything and more. What I would love to see is a recipe planner using their AI that helps you to share ingredients between recipes, or maybe builds some example plans for you and then you can choose from them. title: Does what I want (and more) exceptionally well
body: I have super appreciated this app for years, but was initially put off by the requirement to pay for it again. Then somebody reminded me that seven years is a long time for an app to keep working. For example, I am no longer able to use the Microsoft office suite I purchased for my windows XP machine. Fair reasoning. That said, here are some of the reasons I value this app so highly: The “import recipe from a URL” is simply astonishing. It extracts the important elements for recipes from websites like AllRecipes and the Food Network, while leaving all the ads and commentary out. Everything is completely editable after importing, so if you want to alter the recipe to reflect something you saw in the comments, it’s very easy. The import via OCR (optical character recognition – converting a photo with printed text to digital text) is not quite as simple, but once you get it, it’s fantastic. It allowed me to retain my favorite recipes from my mother’s cookbooks, which were falling apart. I told it which parts of the image were the title, ingredients and steps, and it did the rest. The tags, timer, and “cross-out finished steps” features are the ones I use the most, but this app has loads of other features, also. The interface is very user-friendly and the pro version is an exceptional value.

title: The best app - great features coming soon
body: There’s a few things I really like about this app. - Really easy scanning, with options so you don’t need to type anything manually. Highly intuitive. Not perfect but close. - Best UI I’ve seen in this kind of app. Very pleasant to look at. - Very easy to use print and bulk export options. - One low monthly ($1.5) or yearly ($10) payment gives me access to all the recipes across ALL my devices; most apps charge separately, and while CB might be a tiny bit more expensive in the long run, I won’t be out for a larger lump sum of money if I need to replace my device, want to use a different one, etc. A lot of the features that I feel are missing have already been suggested by other users and are coming soon, hence why I decided to give this app a 5 star rating. BUT personally I’d like to see the following sooner rather than later: -rich text support, as well as font size selection (very important for long or tricky recipes) -recipe cross-referencing (e.g. a sandwich recipe will automatically cross-reference the recipe for the bread it requires) -ingredients substitution and quantity variance support (so that it changes accordingly when scaling the recipe) -quick toggle between recipes -some drag-and-drop options -“pantry management” options to keep track of ingredients easily -Siri/Alexa options so that I don’t have to manipulate the device while handling ingredients. Just getting it to scroll or change pages is enough. -A “family and friends” feature for recipe sharing and quick importing of individual recipes would be lovely.

title: Great app to manage your recipes
body: When a cooking recipe app I was using for many years changed in a way I didn’t like, I started researching for find a new app to manage my recipes. After trying out different apps I found Cookbook is easy to use and did everything I need it to do. They make it easy to enter my recipes from my Word docs and have them in a more convenient format for cooking and baking. When I find other recipes I want try online, the app makes it really easy to import and allows me to customize as I adapt the recipe to make it my own. I really love the way CookBook - Recipe Manager App works.

title: Feature-packed, Elegantly crafted App!
body: For a little over a year, I’ve been only cooking and eating meals that I’ve prepared and so I have a bunch of recipes bookmarked and organized as best as I could manage on Safari but I hate how most recipe sites follow a top-down approach to show the information that I’m looking for in a recipe; summary, ingredients AND THEN steps. I’ve craved for being able to view steps and ingredients side-by-side. This app has that horizontal view and other features that I didn’t even know I needed! The fact that I can import recipes is great, since I have a bunch bookmarked. I love that I can have a shopping list generated for me, while before, I would need to use some of my precious time to do so. I love that you can set timers that defaults to time required for a particular step. I use siri homepod for my timers usually but it’s awesome to have this feature in-app. I’m not sure how much time this app will give me back, but the flow that I had set up for food prep was definitely a process, now… The only time I take is trying to figure out what I want to eat for the week! Love it :)

title: What an improved experience!
body: Holy mackerel, I love the new scanning user interface! This was the greatest leap forward I’ve ever seen in an app. Love, love, love!

title: Game Changing App
body: I don’t often leave reviews, but this app has been a complete game changer for my meal prep. Before installing this app, I would bookmark all the recipes I found online and tried my best to organize them in folders. But digging through a list of titles meant I often skimmed past recipes I loved or struggled to find the recipe I was looking for. This app has completely changed how I approach cooking/meal prep and even lets me share my favorite recipes with friends! I can now quickly import recipes from the internet or recipes scribbled down by my in-laws directly to my cookbook. It’s easy to find what I’m looking for thanks to all the pictures and custom tags (they start you off with some basic ones which was super helpful). And thanks to the shopping list feature I can now quickly plan out my meals for the week and get an organized shopping list that combines the same ingredients across recipes - no more writing everything down on a sticky note and crossing out numbers as multiple recipes start calling for limes. To top it all off, I can even share my recipes/notes with friends whether they have the app or not. But to be honest, now recommending this app to everyone, I absolutely love it. If you like to cook, and have a ton of recipes to store/organize, this is the app for you!

title: Does exactly what I wanted!
body: This app is amazing. It’s a website and phone app that allows you to curate your own recipe book with online recipes. You can take any online recipe link (even the ones that are pay-walled like non appetit) and it scrapes the recipe ingredients and instructions. It puts them in an easy to read format, allows you to scale the recipe for smaller or larger quantities, and allows you to tag the recipe with your own custom tags. You can then search and sort by the tags to make finding the recipes easy. Even more, it lets you add recipes to a meal plan and then use those recipes to generate a shopping list. That feature feels like it’s still a bit in development but it does work. I am at 39 of the 40 free recipes you get and once I fill it, I’ll definitely be buying a lifetime subscription. To the developers: please add a place to add additional links to the recipes. Not just source and video links. Also, make the ingredients list more usable by making it editable over time and not fully refreshed when you add a recipe. It’s common that we add recipes throughout the week and don’t want to lose the edits like what I’ve crossed out cause I already have those things in my kitchen.

title: Fantastic app with one exception.
body: I love this app! It’s simple and easy to use, however one bug would be that on the US standard measurement setting, it changes “cups” to “fluid ounces” even if it’s a dry ingredient!!! It kind of gets confusing and it changes it whether you like it or not. A five star rating would be in order if that was changed!

title: Add multiple photos at the same time please

title: Best cookbook app
body: I transitioned my recipes from one recipe app to this CookBook app. I was pleasantly surprised at how easy it was to use it. Also, the different options in adding a recipe is so easy. A lot of us copy recipes from websites or someone emails you a recipe. This app allows you to copy a recipe from a website simply by copying the that sites URL. It brings in the title of the recipe, the picture of the food, the ingredients and method. You can also change the measuring units. I like to always covert to the measurement to US Standard. It easily converts it. Another feature is the actual link to the site which is displayed within the recipe in the app. If there is a video attached to the recipe it also automatically pulls it in. There are so many features that comes with this app that was not included in my previous app. You have a choice of using different methods to copy a recipe. If the recipe is in pdf or some type of a written form, you can easily copy the recipe using this app. Of course, you can also manually add a recipe with ease. I’m sold! To the developers, we’ll done!

title: Just what I wanted -

title: unethical business practices
body: I paid for this app two years ago when it was not a subscription service. If I had known it would be turned into a subscription I would have just used a free app, or even saved pdfs to a drive on my computer. Now I am being forced, after purchasing an item, to pay for that same item AGAIN? When Microsoft updates it’s operating system, does your old windows 7 stop working? In what universe is it reasonable to ask someone to pay forty dollars for a “lifetime subscription” to something they’ve already purchased? How do I know that in two more years, the app won’t decide that they need to add new features and charge me another forty dollars, why not a hundred this time? Giving old users a free lifetime subscription is the only thing that makes sense in this context. I used to recommend this app to people, now I’m just going to uninstall it. I can’t spend more of my money on a company with such unethical business practices. I would recommend everyone considering this purchase to reconsider based on this review as well.

title: A Great Recipe App
body: UPDATE: The app is moving to a subscription basis. It’s worth it! Just $9.99 a year for some of the best functionality I’ve found in recipe apps. Developers are highly responsive to questions and feedback which I love. You can’t go wrong with this app. ORIGINAL REVIEW: I’m really loving this app. There’s a little bit of a learning curve, especially when it comes to importing via OCR and to viewing the recipes for use, but it only took me a few times to really start to get the hang of it. It’s a full-featured app and also includes meal planning (more on that later) that lets me finally pull together all those bookmarks, screenshots, printed recipes, pieces of paper, and notecards that I have all over the place. Until now, I’ve relied primarily on bookmarks for web recipes or a collection of big white mailing envelopes that are labelled on the outside (main, veggies, cake, etc) with my bits of paper tucked inside. But, finding something based on a specific ingredients or function? Not so easy. Well, this app not only has tags that you can filter, it allows you to make as many custom tags as you want. I’ve got tags by pan size, type of dish, key ingredients, function, you name it. Now I can find baked goods that use oatmeal or quick breads with bananas and applesauce. Or, I can just browse the thumbnails for inspiration. Getting recipes in will take time but is so easy. Importing from the web is a snap as the app syncs well with most web formats for recipes. Sometimes, it will capture the information but will need to editing work because the website was not a standard recipe form. That’s okay because I didn’t have to bounce back and forth typing or copying and pasting. OCR is pretty sound. It took me a few tries to get the hang of cropping for each section. You can add to ingredients and methods as well - great for dealing with a two-column image when ingredients run across columns or methods run onto a second page. It even handled a good chunk of my hand-written recipes as well. And, of course, you can always type in recipes if need be. The app will automatically import a picture if there’s one on a website recipe. Otherwise, you’ll need to add your own which isn’t hard at all. Take a picture, save it to your photos, then import it from your library. Bingo! When inputting recipes, you sometimes have multiple things that go together but are prepared separately with their own list of ingredients. Take cakes, for example, that have the cake layers, a filling, and possibly a frosting all in one recipe. Well, you can separate those in your ingredient list. Each ingredient has a blank line between. You can put something like “Cake Layers:” with a line return and then the ingredients for the cake, followed by “Filling:” with those ingredients, and then “Buttercream/Icing/Frosting:” followed by those ingredients. The key is having that colon - the app reads it as a heading and formats it in the ingredient list. Same thing for Methods - you can create headings as long as you use a colon after the heading followed by 3 line returns (specific to Methods) and the app will format headings for you. Very cool! Using this to bake the first time, I clicked the forward wedge that is located just under the name of the recipe. That will put you in a screen that has the ingredients on the left and the first step of your recipe. Tap on the right side of the methods frame to advance. I hated it because I like to see everything at once. Problem solved! Just tap on “Method” in the lower right of the main screen for each recipe and you get a full 2-column view. I haven’t used the meal planner. It’s got a good interface, but is a little less customizable than the recipes. I’m on a meal plan that has three meals that alternate with three snacks. The meals list fine, the snacks not so much. I always end up with Breakfast, Snack, Snack, Snack, Lunch, Dinner - no matter what order I actually enter the meals. It’s not a deal breaker but, for me, is a feature flaw that makes it difficult to use. If you’re just using this to plan for your week, though, it’s very easy and even lets you build a shopping list. I’ve tried dozens of recipe apps and have ended up deleting the free ones and returning the paid ones every time. Until this app - it’s well worth the price, doesn’t have hidden in-app charges (like a subscription - I hate those!), and has a beautiful interface that makes it fun to use. Plus, I can use it across all my devices - such a deal! I highly recommend this app if you’re looking for a way to store all those miscellaneous recipes you’ve bookmarked, clipped, written, or otherwise collected over the years. It’s a real winner.

title: Love CB
body: Thanks to CB I no longer have a messy recipe collection in boxes, drawers or stuffed in cabinet corners. I have an organized electronic collection I can share easily. Treasured family recipes are safe and available to all generations of family cooks.

title: Love, love, love this app. Don’t hesitate. Download it.
body: I absolutely love this app. It’s great for storing all of my recipes, for meal planning and for shopping. I do wish they made it slightly easier to share recipes with people who aren’t on the app. A social network kind of function would be great, too. I’d love to share recipes with friends and family.

title: Definitely Worth the $5
body: I’m a big fan of this app and tell everyone I know that this app is very beneficial for those of us who are semi-avid chefs. If there was an option to make a grocery list (where it combines selected ingredient lists) by adding certain recipes you’ve gathered. Like if I don’t write a list; I will sometimes find myself going through the different recipes I have to see what else I need to buy. Other than that though.. no issues 👍🏼

title: Best cookbook app
body: This is the best! Easy to copy and paste links in here and easy to keep your recipes organized. Worth it!!

title: User Friendly Interface/Visually Appealing
body: Update 10/2020 Still the best recipe saving app to me. I tend to “pin” recipes never giving a thought about the longevity of that “pin”. I wanted to make this great cornbread recipe (the best ever made) I pinned a few years back. Well, the link is broken. The originating website no longer exists. I was quite upset with myself for not saving it. However, I decided to check my Cookbook app in case I did happen to upload that recipe I pinned. I did!!!! I forgot that I slowly started to upload pinned favorite recipes a year ago whenever I had time. Well, now I am making time because websites and blogs are not forever. Must have app. 2019 Finally found a recipe saving app that has everything I wanted. Easy to import online recipes with minimal time spent fixing entries. Easy to navigate. Great interface that is visually appealing. Ability to share recipes. Timer feature inside recipe steps is ingenious. Tagging is simple. Nutritional information not always imported but easily added with copy and paste. The app and website version works without any delays or crashes so far. A great investment for those who love to cook, organize recipes, have photos for each recipe step, or meal plan.

title: Finally cataloging my favorite printed recipes!
body: This app makes collecting recipes pretty painless, including ones you might be photographing from your collection of vintage church cookbooks. The OCR hasn’t really failed me yet. I also like the feature that recognizes a recipe URL on your clipboard when you open the app. Meal planning is fairly easy, too, although I wish you could add a manual note for some meals (e.g. “leftovers”) without having to have a recipe saved

title: Incredibly easy
body: I previously copied, cut, pasted recipes to word processor and saved. Now they are readily available and easy to share. I haven’t found a site it couldn’t import 5 stars

title: Best Recipe Manager!
body: I love that this app doesn’t come bloated with a bunch of suggested recipes. I have my own recipes, I just need somewhere to keep them! The web clipper is awesome, ocr works beautifully to import from my cookbooks. Tagging helps me find what I’m looking for. The app is simple but perfectly executed.

title: Works Across Platforms
body: When the recipe app I was using, Pepper Plate, switched to a monthly subscription service (after no updates for many years), I looked at all the top reviewed options available. One of the top competitors required purchasing on every platform I used, and it was not cheap. Compared with Cookbook, it seemed bloated with extras. Cookbook has worked flawlessly since I started using it. Is it without quirks? No. But name one app that isn’t. I can access it from any device, it’s well organized, and it does a great job importing from other sites. I think this is currently the best app for storing recipes.

title: I love the Cookbook app.
body: My son hooked me up with this app and I am addicted. I have several recipe sites that email me recipes. I look through them and then save the ones I like to Cookbook. Then when I am in the mood for say cauliflower or eggplant I just type that item into search and it brings up all the cauliflower recipes I have saved. Then my grocery list is a snap.

title: Phenomenal app!
body: While I am new to the app, I’m excited to discover all that I haven’t found on it yet. I love that I don’t have to type out all the recipes. I love that I can copy a URL and it recognizes that I have it waiting when I open the app. I love that it will convert quantities according to serving sizes. I will be sharing my love for this app wherever I can! Well done! And, thank you!!

title: Love this app!
body: I used a different app for years and was ok with it until they went to a yearly subscription. That’s a HUGE turn off for me. I found this one and have really enjoyed it since. The import process was so simple and fast. I love that I can just take a picture of a recipe, edit very little and it’s ready to go instead of typing out the entire recipe. Customizing the tags is also nice to have and easy to do. I have recently started using the meal planner function, which I have to say is WAY better than the last app I used so I never used it before now. It pops up a button on the bottom of the home page that says “dinner” and it takes you straight to the recipe for the day. Genius! The developers are responsive and open to feedback and suggestions for future updates, which is appreciated. I highly recommend this app!

title: They thought of everything!
body: It's quite amazing all the features packed in this app. Timers, checking off ingredients, scaling the recipe (e.g. make it for 2 when recipe was given for 1), and most importantly how you can import recipes from the web! That's the killer feature for me.

title: Great app👍🏽
body: 5 dollars were worth it.

title: New obsess-worthy cooking app
body: This has been my new go-to app bc I’ve been able to combine all my favorite recipes from my favorite cooking apps, magazines, websites, and my own sources.

title: Helpful
body: This app makes storing and finding recipes so convenient! I easily imported old family recipes, and magazine recipes. Also, instead of hundreds of bookmarked recipes on the internet, I imported those too. It’s simple to edit and add notes; it converts measurements instantly when you choose a different number of servings, so you don’t have to do a lot of math. You can share the recipes too. I use it every day.

title: My Go To Recipe Book
body: I am converting all of my favorite recipes to this app. The various capture and input methods make this easy to build an integrated recipe book. It takes a bit of experimenting to learn the various capture methods but once you’ve got it you won’t forget as the app is self directing on how to capture and tune your recipes. Capture from your browser is very easy and my go to method if possible. The OCR method works well and is the way I captured many of my oldest printed recipes or from the recipe books that line my kitchen shelf. This app works and it gives me my recipes at my fingertips wherever I go and when I use it in the kitchen it does not switch off when I turn my back like other apps that I have used like to do. It sounds simple but this can be very irritating if your hands are knee deep in ingredients. Try it - you will like it.

title: Best app ever
body: This app changed the game for me in terms of cooking and keeping my recipes all in one convenient place. So easy to use and would use it time and again.

title: Favorite
body: It has quickly become one of my favorite apps ever,

title: Best recipe app
body: I searched all the recipe apps and this is the best one. It works on multiple platforms, not just your phone. It has OCR so you can take pictures of recipes and input them into your collection. For the laptop, there’s an extension to automatically “clip” a recipe from a website into your collection. It’s great! You can set timers within recipes as you make them. You can halve or double recipes. You can do meal planning and construct grocery lists. It’s a reasonable price for all you get and it’s great that you don’t have to pay a monthly fee. I refuse to have to pay each month to organize and access my own recipes! These developers get it and have made a very user-friendly app.

title: Love this app
body: This makes cooking and shopping fun!

title: Very Impressed
body: By far the most advanced cookbook app I’ve used!

title: Love this!
body: I looked and looked for an app that I could create my own recipes and my own meal plan, and this is it. I’m so excited!! Can’t wait to use all the features!

title: Best. App. Ever.!
body: For a person like me who considers herself to have limited computer skills, this app is amazingly easy to use. Well worth the $4.99. In the last few days I have uploaded recipes that were ripped out of magazines and have been in my corner cabinet for years. ( I use them of course) yet now there is no more clutter. I shared my recipes via email in matter of a minute by PDF file, and I just uploaded in less than 30 seconds a recipe from the Food Network. I feel like a computer wiz and just LOVE this app. One of the best investments I ever made. One recommendation is that you read the recipes after you up load them Bc sometimes it will read 4 cups when it means 1/4cup. There can be a glitch with the backslash.

title: BEST recipe collection app ever
body: Pros: - well-organized for recipe steps/instructions - ingredients and steps on same screen - takes you step by step with you hit the “start” button; will even read it to you - cross off ingredients as you go so that you know you’ve got it covered - allows you to input different pictures for every step of the instructions - creates grocery lists based on your menu plan - grocery lists organized by aisle - OCR scan for recipes from a book - imports from other cooking websites - beautiful graphics and organization Cons: - doesn’t seem as popular as Paprika, so I hope they keep on providing updates and fixes and won’t fall off the radar - doesn’t suggest new recipes (though, that’s what the internet and cookbooks are for); this is purely a recipe collection app, not a recipe suggestion - needs feature where you can input the ingredients you have and it will find a recipe for you that can use your ingredients

title: I love this meal planning app!
body: This app is worth every penny you pay for it. It helps you not only plan your meals but compile your recipes into one place where they can be efficiently organized.

title: I’ve been using cookbook for almost a year
body: I live this app! Im always collecting recipes. Before I used Cookbook, I had magazines all over the place and no way to organize the recipes that interested me. Cookbook has helped me to reduce the clutter a s to be able to find the recipes I’m looking for. It’s easy to import recipes from websites and mailing lists, too!

title: The Best Kitchen Accessory!!!
body: My husband purchased this app for me a couple of Christmases ago. I now have this on every device! It’s seriously become my right hand! The app is absolutely superb! I have to admit, when I received the app- I wasn’t too excited. I’ve been accustomed to the old fashioned cookbooks- ones you can flip through by hand. He knew I was looking for something to organize my recipes, and after much research- he asked me to just give it a shot.... And I’m so thrilled I did! The recipes are SOOO simple to upload! You can either type them in, copy a link from a website (this works on about 95% of sites I’ve tried- I think the key to it is the website needs to have a “recipe card” on their page- which most do), and they have a way to import via a picture! You take a picture of your recipe, mark where your title, ingredients, etc are and it uploads it! Love it! The app allows you to schedule your recipes for each night (I’ve never used this feature, but I could see where it would be helpful!), add recipes to a favorite section (I use this sometimes to keep track of which recipes I’m going to be using for the week)... and the best part?!?! The cooking portion!!!!!!!! Y’all! The designers of this app did it right! You can turn your phone or tablet sideways- you then have a recipe card on one side that you can flip through as you go, and your ingredients are on the right. What helps tremendously is the fact that you can click which ingredients you have used! There is an option to hide the used-ingredients, so you’re only left with what you haven’t used yet. It helps so much in being able to take quick glances and see what measure of a certain ingredient you need! The app also allows you to set multiple timers at one time! The app is just all around amazing! And the best $4.99 you can spend on making your time in the kitchen a success! It’s just very efficient! The developers are even rockstars! I messaged them when I first got the app with a weird issue I was having, and they had it fixed within a moment’s notice! Amazing! To the developers: One suggestion, if you ever look to modify the app at all- if there could be a bookmark button, or a way to toggle between 2 recipes at a time- that would be awesome!!!! For now, I just switch recipes and find the step number I was on and re-mark which ingredients I’ve used... but, again, if you ever look to make and modifications- this mod would be my vote 😉 Thank you Cookbook App for making such a wonderful product!

title: Beautiful app with all the functionality
body: After spending admittedly too much time researching and trying out the top meal planning apps out there, CookBook was by far the best compared to the others (mainly MealLime, Pepperplate, Paprika and Plan to Eat). I was nervous about paying up front to try this app out, and now I’m literally looking every time I open the app for a donate button because of how great my experience with it is. Best Features: - stunning design (so beautiful to use) - incredibly friendly to use - import works with every source I’ve tried so far! - love the view as list or tile features - love the shopping list feature - love being able to scale the recipes - love full feature support on the app and web - cooking mode is so simple and clean - SO worth the one-time fee Feature Wishlist: (mostly just cherry on top requests I would gladly help fund if there were ways to!) - wish could generally assign meals to a week and check off as go (vs. assigning to a specific day) - wish could integrate with services like Instacart - wish could integrate with services like MyFitnessPal or Apple Health - wish could do bulk import - wish didn’t have to open and save with clipper - wish could sort by things like date added - wish imported all photos and was a little easier to assign those photos to steps in the recipe Compared to other apps: - MealLime is limited to their recipes (which were quite bland and flavorless) or pay up for adding your own and then you lose half of the features that make the app useful like built in nutrition facts, organized shopping lists, scaling recipes, etc) - Pepperplate is moving to subscription model, but their features barely work (almost never can import cleanly from another source), and you don’t get feature parity on mobile and web - Paprika’s design just made my eyes hurt it was so busy. A lot of features, but the intuitiveness of finding and using them all was poor. - Plan to Eat had nice design, but it wasn’t as nice as CookBook and the continual service fee model didn’t seem worth it. You end up paying so much more for the same core functionality.

title: Quality product
body: Good product, worth every penny.

title: Thoughtfully designed, amazingly functional, beautiful
body: This is the best recipe management app I’ve tried (and I’ve spent a lot of time testing them out!). Incredibly thoughtful features—hyperlinked timers from the text of the recipe, link from the home screen to today’s planned meal, accurate ocr for print cookbook recipes—and clean, intentional design to pack them all in in a way that’s intuitive to use and visually pleasing.

title: LOVE THIS APP!
body: I’ve wanted to develop recipes to compile into a cookbook or for a newsletter for a WHILE. This app isn’t just EASY to use, the out put is so PRETTY too! It takes ‘my work’ to a new level without me having to do a lot of extra formatting other apps require! My ONLY suggestion would be to offer an option to create a cookbook of ‘my own’ recipes from the app (and cookbook app please contact me if you want more ideas/feedback around this!) I’d LOVE TO give you all my thoughts and pay for what you put together!!

title: BUY IT
body: I had very high expectations for this app and it exceeded them. My favorite part is the Surprise Me button, which randomly selects a recipe for you.

title: Almost perfect
body: First thing is first, this app is excellent. Low one time payment, no ads, no extra surprises. You get more than you pay for in my opinion, as a notebook and pen would be approximately the same price and have only an inkling of this app’s capability. I have found importing recipes from online sources to be very easy, as is creating your own recipes manually. I have not used the other methods yet. One of the main reasons I chose this app was the ability to have an integrated meal planner and grocery list to save time and money at the store. This is where I believe this app can be improved. If you have a habitual routine for meals or a meal plan, this app is tedious to plan for the coming week. I like to enjoy a smoothie everyday for breakfast, and adding the recipe to each morning of each coming week is an annoying process. I suggest a simple added feature to fix this: a repeat function when adding a meal to any given day. What I believe would be a more difficult solution for the developers, but better for users like myself, would be a weekly meal plan instead of a calendar. This simple Sun thru Sat (with no associated date) setup could easily list your meals and would automatically remain unchanged from week to week, which would reduce the amount of time users would need to spend editing a new weekly plan. And if some users are on a strict meal plan, they would never have to update a weekly plan after a one time set up. I would also like to add that users creating a variety of meals would still spend the same amount of time editing their meal plan for the coming week, so there is no disadvantage to this new setup. This is just my personal suggestion on how to improve this app, I would be happy to correspond with the developers if they find this an interesting feature. Again, as is, this is a fantastic app and I highly recommend it.

title: Love this app
body: I’ve been cooking for more than 50 years and have a cookbook collection that covers 25’ of shelving. I love to cook and was thrilled when my daughter suggested Cookbook it’s an incredible app. So far Ive added over a 1000+ recipes to the app great for shopping and wonderful to access the recipes without going through 20-30 cookbooks to find them!

title: Overall really like it!
body: Overall I really like the app and I have recommended it to others. Its easy, love the import and tag options and I am just getting into the meal planning. My only issues are for some recipes I cannot get the ingredients to stay in cups and it switches it to oz or another measurement. I have tried different things but doesnt help. This is only a few recipes this has been an issue with. The other issue is I wished I could backup on my computer instead of on phone. However, I did email it to myself so it does accomplish it. My complaints are more annoying then anything and overall I am very happy with the app!! I recommend giving it a try!

body: Really nice app to organize and share recipes. Easy to use. Wish there was an option to send your entire Cook Book to someone.

title: The best.
body: Love this app, and love that you get all the functionality for a one time fee, not some ridiculous monthly subscription. There are better apps if you want to search for new recipes BUT if you’re looking for a clean, lovely recipe manager, this is the best. The import function works well—my handwritten recipes always take a tiny bit of editing, but I blame my own goofy handwriting for that. The recipe clip tool is AMAZING. I LOVE that I can sync it across all my devices—my iPhone, my MacBook, and the cheap Android tablet I keep in the kitchen solely for recipes, to cook around. I can find a great recipe randomly while out, save it, but the ingredients, and have it pop up on my kitchen tablet when I get home. Beautiful. Suggestion for the next update: an IBSN search function so I can get rid of all my random cookbooks once and for all <3

title: Love it!
body: So easy and quick to add recipes from different sources, share them with friends, add photos as I make the recipes, and have my ingredients needed right at my fingertips when I have a recipe impulse in the grocery store! Fun to thumb through pictures to decide what to make! And no more bulky cookbooks!

title: The Best Recipe Book Ever
body: I love it 😍 Just what I was looking for & better

title: The BEST recipe manager app for iOS. HANDS DOWN.
body: I’ve tried several free apps, several paid apps, and this has been the best so far. It has everything. Being able to also log on a computer was very important to me. Sometimes, it’s faster to type on a laptop, or take photos of a recipe, or pulling recipes off of webpages, instead of inputting manually using your iPhone. This has all of these features, plus more! To top it off, their customer service IS SO fast with replying to their support emails, and resolution was extremely quick. Will never use another recipe app again. This is the best, and only one I’ll use.

title: Tried all alternatives- this is the best option
body: After loosing all of my recipes with Zest, hating the user interface in Copymethat and Paprika, I’ve finally found the Cookbook app and it’s perfect. I recommended it to the large russian speaking cooking community and whoever downloaded it - loves it as well.

title: True “Cookbook” and more ⭐️⭐️⭐️
body: I don’t like leaving reviews. But this one deserves more than 5 stars, nay, Apple needs to create a different category just for this app. In my MANY years of using iPhone and numerous apps, I’ve never seen such a thoroughly-thought-through app. The developer must have done his homework very well for us users. Every turn you find the developer’s thoughtful, clever, intelligent, and useful addition. There is nothing “I wish it was...”. What we could ever think of as the best recipe/meal planner app, this app has it all. The functionality of this app deserves “the App of the Year” easily. And I am not exaggerating even a bit how so well designed app this is and how so well it is working. The OCR is the best part of this app for me. Finally, I could add my favorite recipes from my cookbooks that had been on my bookshelf for ages without being organized. I am importing all my favorite recipes from websites and from my old recipe apps (including Paprika). Cookbook covers all realms of a cookbook ought to be. I finally found a place where all my recipes will be saved. I am not sure how many times I shouted “wow” while building up my cookbook here - there are no unnecessary part in this app. So clean and neat, beautiful and functional, & easy and delightful to use. I’ve never said “thank you” to app developers and this is my first one - THANK YOU for this app which you created with all your effort and time. Your app truly deserves the name “Cookbook”!

title: Fantastic!
body: Don’t sell yourself short by downloading a free app. Save yourself the headache and get this one. From the best recipe import engine on any app that I’ve seen, to meal planning, to shopping and sharing, this is the best cookbook app out there and well worth the money.

title: Good job developers! This is great.
body: I recently started the Keto diet and was gifted a Keto book. I immediately started looking for apps that could translate a picture into the correct input for recipe creation. This app fits the bill and is the only one on the store that does this. Also the other features like meal planning and generation of grocery lists is great. I just generated my first list for the first week of meal prep. You can select dates to generate lists which is good. Lots of functionality wrapped up in this app! Couple of wants... -Ability to export import recipes into MyFitnessPal. So far I could get this to work. -Ability to quick edit the grocery list items. I discovered an error in one of the items and needed to correct it. However, if you correct the source recipe you have to regenerate the grocery list. -Ability to share the grocery list with my wife. We are logged in to the same account but the grocery list does not show up in her app even after syncing.

title: Great Paprika alternative
body: I got fed up after losing years worth of recipes on Paprika, so I figured I’d try this app out. I had a question about the app before my purchase, and I was contacted within hours by the kindest lady. This was an instant purchase, and I’m loving it so far. I’m a professional cook, and I love the leftovers option, mostly as inspiration. Thank you all, keep up the great work.

title: Search no further
body: I was fed up with our old recipe saving app. I decided I wanted something that was going to work right, I was ready to pay extra for it. It was so worth it! It’s so easy to use! It has such a pretty, and simple layout. I love that you can input recipes in multiple ways. The tags for recipes is so handy! Sharing recipes is easier. I haven’t tried the leftovers option yet, but that looks interesting! Thanks for making this app ❤️

title: Great for moving between phone and desktop!
body: I love that this app allows me to enter recipes in from my desktop. The tool to convert from a blog post to a recipe could be better. Sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn’t. But this is my favorite recipe app.

title: Amazing!!!
body: I love this App! I was using multiple apps for the recipes I was storing and not really loving any of them. To add to my frustration using multiple apps, made it more difficult to remember which app had the specific recipe I was hunting for. The solution was to find one app that would import from anywhere with photos and have the allowance of notes I could add once a recipe was made. Cookbook fit my needs perfectly! It has flawlessly imported every single recipe I wanted in it thus far. It was well worth the money for this app. I did have to save photos a couple times to add to the recipes because for whatever reason they wouldn’t import. But it’s so easy to save a photo and then add it, I don’t consider this an issue at all. The organization and beautiful photo gallery display for your recipes makes you want to cook the minute you open it! I love the calendar and shopping list that help you figure out what you want to cook for the week and how many ingredients you will need to buy. I’m not so sure about the pdf import feature. It seemed like it had a little trouble reading my recipes when I tried importing them this way. The ingredients weren’t coming out with the right measurements. I fixed that by using copy and paste. All fixed! I haven’t tried the photo import feature but I do have some recipes ripped from magazines that I will at some point import. I am very excited to try this feature so I don’t have to type the whole recipe out myself. The sharing feature is as amazing as the rest of this app! You can choose from several formats to share from. The recipes look absolutely beautiful in an email and text. Making it a delight to share my recipes with friends and family. This app is simply amazing and I am so glad I found it. Thank you for making such a perfect app!

title: Love most of it so far
body: I just got this and am still working on how I want to use it. So far I love that I can snap pictures to import recipes and not have to type it all. It’s easy to add pictures of the dishes and steps. I can make up my own tags so I can organize things in my own way. I can add notes. There’s a way to back up what I’ve entered. I can share it on my devices. And I love that there’s no subscription fee which really turned me off of other app choices. Things I’m still trying to work out is editing the data after an import can be cumbersome. Sometimes it adds funky characters that I cannot get rid of no matter what I try, including deleting and adding manually. And I wish I could print an index card format vs a full page pdf. I’m also leery about having a full database of recipes on my phone. I don’t want to buy more phone memory just for recipes! But I have yet to see if that’s really going to be a problem or not. Overall I’m really pleased.

title: Wow. You people nailed it.
body: This app is phenomenal. I was brainstorming features I would want in a recipe, meal, and shopping list planner app of my own creation when I came across this app. To see each idea and more come to life in a sleek, well-designed, intuitive, and powerful manner in this app was euphoric. It is better than I could have ever dreamed of! Everything I wanted and more. Good price made it more attractive than other apps. I love the abilities to import recipes from pictures, other recipe formats, and file types. The user interface was easy to grasp and follow even on my first recipe import. I would love to see some sort of bulk import (API?) in the future, but most of my saved recipes are pictures anyway. I’m not sure if there is some sort of syncing family plan where recipes, plans, and lists can be synced between linked user accounts or devices, but that would be awesome too. Lots of praise and kudos for this app!!!!

title: Must have app
body: This is the first app that I saw allowing access to recipes offline. It’s super easy to copy any recipe to this platform. Love, love, love this app. This has made my life so much easier!

title: Best App for Recipes
body: I have put off making a review for far too long on this app. This app is amazing. I have downloaded almost every single recipe app and none of them compare at all to this one. It is so easy to use. The drop down menus, scrolling and changing pages happens fast and smooth. The font, graphics and layouts is truly appealing to the eyes. It makes you want to cook. Here are some of my favorite features. Leftovers 🥦🍅🧀🍐🥔 You can search leftover ingredients that you have and it will bring up the recipes that include these ingredients, perfect when you’re tired to think of what to make. Favorites ❤️ It helps so much to come up with ideas of what to cook using your favorites. You can search the main foods/ingredients you have and just like the leftovers, it’ll pull up all the recipes with your ingredients and you can go through and heart your favorites. Under the favorites tag you have a gorgeous list of your recipes. Now you’re ready, you have meal ideas with the foods you’ll actually use that week, and will feel prepared with a ton of your recipes and inspiration to cook! Meal Planner 🍽 If you’re into details, then the meal planner covers that. You can set as many recipes to your breakfast, lunch, snack, appetizer, dinner and of course dessert 😋🥧 Pictures + Tags 📷 It’s easy to have an image for every recipe so it looks amazing scrolling through them. You can create tags so your collection of recipes are super organized. Scanning 📚 Any paper recipes or screenshots can easily be scanned and added to the app... and for how much? Free. Amazing. I’m impressed by how much the developers have done to improve, improve and improve this app. Download it, give it a chance, try it out and I bet you’re gonna love it. Veronica C
